subject: Geo performance & residency follow-up — NimbleHealth (post-demo)
messages:
From: Alex White <alex@nimblehealth.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo recap — regional performance questions

Thanks for the demo this morning, Markus/Kim — very helpful. A few follow-ups from our infra and security teams so we can scope the pilot: 

1) Latency targets: we need an internal target for 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency for short clinical prompts (~50 tokens). Can you propose realistic numbers for US/EU/APAC?
2) Concurrency and throughput: expected concurrent authorship for our use-case is ~80 concurrent active users, peak ~150. Curious about recommended concurrency buckets and any guidance on burst behavior.
3) Streaming and web sockets: our RN team will stream partial results to the UI — does Redwood’s streaming behavior change latency/throughput expectations?
4) Data residency: EU PHI-like records must remain in EU. For APAC, we may require a co-located region (Singapore) or a private deployment. Any constraints we should know?

Can you send a short SLO matrix and a list of what’s achievable on hosted vs dedicated vs private? Also share any logs/retention implications for audit.

Appreciate a short action list and next steps.

— Alex
Lead Platform Engineer, NimbleHealth

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Alex White <alex@nimblehealth.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — regional performance questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I captured answers below and attached a concise performance matrix and a sample network-trace bundle for APAC. TL;DR: we can meet tight US latencies on hosted; EU residency requires either Dedicated (EU-backed compute) or Private; APAC will need regional capacity (Singapore) or Dedicated with burst routing.

SLO proposals (95th percentile, end-to-end request seen by your UI for ~50 token responses):
- US (us-west/us-east): 95p <= 160ms (short responses, streaming enabled)
- EU (Frankfurt): 95p <= 220ms (when pinned to EU-hosted model variant)
- APAC (Singapore): 95p <= 300ms (cold path cross-region falls back to ~420ms)

Throughput & concurrency guidance:
- Sustained concurrency target: 80 concurrent active users = ~160 concurrent inference requests (users may open background requests).
- Recommended headroom: reserve capacity for 2x peak (so plan for 300 concurrent requests to avoid queuing).
- Burst behavior: hosted supports short bursts (~10–30s) via shared capacity but can't guarantee 0-queue for sustained bursts; Dedicated provides burst pools and guaranteed concurrency slices.

Streaming specifics:
- Streaming (chunked token streaming / WebSocket) adds negligible per-token CPU overhead; however, tail latency variance increases with network hops. For streaming UI we recommend: smaller initial chunk sizes, aggressive KV cache for repeated prefixes, and a local jitter buffer in the client to smooth token arrival. Measured differences: streaming vs non-streaming end-to-end 95p delta ~ +20–40ms depending on region.

Data residency & audit:
- EU residency requirement: logs, KV cache, and persisted traces for EU customer accounts can be constrained to EU-only storage on Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be region-pinned for model execution but audit logs may still be retained in control-plane territories unless you choose Dedicated/Private.
- APAC: we can provision Singapore region under Dedicated; Private is the only path for on-prem.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll send a focused SLO matrix and two sample capacity scenarios (sustained + burst) — attachment: nimblehealth-performance-matrix-20261105.xlsx
2) Kimberly will follow up with an ops playbook for streaming clients and sample WebSocket settings (cc’d).
3) We’ll share an anonymized APAC network trace (attachment) and our measuring script so you can run a few client probes.

If this looks OK I can schedule a 30-min ops deep-dive tomorrow with Connor to walk the matrix and map Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta.

— Markus Klein
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[attachments: nimblehealth-performance-matrix-20261105.xlsx (xlsx); nimblehealth-network-traces-APAC-pcap.zip (zip)]

Thanks, Markus — this is helpful. A couple clarifying points from security/compliance: 

- For EU residency, we need confirmation that KV cache and any model input artifacts are never written to object storage outside EU. If hosted can’t guarantee that, Dedicated is fine — please call that out in the matrix.
- Retention: audit logs for compliance audits must be retained for 7 years and available via export. Is that supported today for Dedicated?
- APAC: our legal team prefers a private deployment for Singapore but is open to a Dedicated proof-of-concept if the cost is reasonable.

Also — can you add a row to the SLO matrix with expected tokens/sec for each regional capacity tier (small/medium/large)? That will help our infra sizing.

We’d like the ops deep-dive tomorrow at 11:00 CET if that works for your team.

— Sarah
Head of Infrastructure, NimbleHealth

Sarah — great questions. Short answers and where I updated the attached matrix: 

1) KV cache & object writes: for Hosted we do use control-plane metadata in our US control region; we cannot guarantee that ephemeral KV cache never crosses control-plane regions. For strict EU-only write guarantees (including KV metadata and persisted traces) you must choose Dedicated (EU tenant) or Private. I added a bold ‘EU-residency safe’ column in the sheet.

2) Retention: Dedicated supports configurable audit-log retention and exports (we support 7+ years via our long-term archival tier). I added a note with the retention SLA and export formats (JSON/NDJSON).

3) APAC path: Private is the cleanest legal fit. Dedicated SG region is our low-lift option for a POC — cost estimate included as a delta in the matrix.

4) Tokens/sec by capacity tier: added rows for small/medium/large (approx tokens/sec for your LLM family, measured on seq=64): small=1200 tps, medium=3600 tps, large=8800 tps. These are rough estimates — Connor can run a tailored perf run during the ops meeting.

I scheduled the ops deep-dive: Tomorrow 11:00 CET / 02:00 PST — invite sent to this thread. Agenda: SLO matrix walkthrough, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, streaming client best practices, initial POC plan. Connor will bring the perf scripts.

If you want, Kimberly and I can draft an MPO (mutual plan of operations) to lock the pilot milestones and success criteria.

Thanks — talk tomorrow.

— Markus
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
